relations.subject: Kazi Dawa Samdup
relations.evidence: In 1874 he joined the Bhutia Boarding School in Darjeeling where he impressed the headmaster Rai Bahadur Sarat Chandra Das.

relations.subject: Kazi Dawa Samdup
relations.evidence: His Tibetan teacher was Ugyen Gyatso, a lama from the Pemayangtse monastery in West Sikkim.

relations.subject: Kazi Dawa Samdup
relations.evidence: During his stay in Bhutan, he became a pupil of a learned and ascetic lama, Lopen Tshampa Norbu (Slob dpon Mtshams pa Nor bu) d. 1916 of Punakha from whom he received initiation and instruction.

relations.subject: Alexandra David-Néel
relations.evidence: In 1912 Sidkeong Tulku Namgyal entrusted his "confidante and spiritual sister" Alexandra David-Néel to Kazi Dawa Samdup to be her a guide, interpreter and teacher of Tibetan.

relations.subject: Kazi Dawa Samdup
relations.evidence: In 1920, he was appointed teacher in Tibetan at the University of Calcutta.

relations.subject: Kazi Dawa Samdup
relations.evidence: Kazi Dawa Samdup is probably best known for his path-breaking translations of Tibetan texts which were later edited and published by W. Y. Evans-Wentz.

relations.subject: Kazi Dawa Samdup
relations.evidence: With Sir John Woodroffe: Shrîchakrasambhâra Tantra: A Buddhist Tantra (Dem-chog Tantra). First published in 1918–1919.
